messages.subject: "Disconnected from server" error on blank grey page when deploying shinyApp on shinyapps.io. Works fine locally.
messages.subject_clean: "Disconnected from server" error on blank grey page when deploying shinyApp on shinyapps.io. Works fine locally.
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am able to have my Shiny app work locally, but it gives me the error: "Disconnected from server" on a blank, grey page when I deploy it to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> to share.  Here is my code:

library(dplyr)
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(plotOutput("plot1"))

server <- function(input, output) {
  MY_DATA <- read.csv("/Users/'myusername'/Desktop/APPTRY/MY_DATA.csv")
    output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
      plot(MY_DATA$Charge, MY_DATA$X..of.Claims)
    })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

My app.R file is also saved in the path that I cite within the read.csv command.

Any help would be appreciated!!

I am using fileInput control in my commercial project deployed to shinyapps.io Several files are not uploaded to the server and this error message is logged: Error
/usr/share/luajit/share/lua/5.1/lapis/application.lua:65: attempt to index local 'curr' (a boolean value)

Traceback

Looks like the upload fails for some specific file content (strange, what's the difference for the upload tool what content uploaded file has), I found a similar issue reported by other users and the fix was to remove ampersand character from the file! When I run the same application locally file gets uploaded correclty, so for me it seems to be shinyapps.io  problem. I can also reproduce the problem on one of the examples that I found on shiny/rstudio tutorial (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/tree/master/009-upload)

Any help would be appreciated.

regards, Adam

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the tip, this turned out be not a bug, but a design limit.

Here is the drop down list

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-JL2_tMYX3zQ/WV6iDMn220I/AAAAAAAAAEA/A0oD_pUKYEAoha0p7fEAP8WLH5gN4zaCwCLcBGAs/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2017-07-06%2Bat%2B4.46.54%2BPM.png>

So it cannot differentiate two accounts in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> with same app name, the designer probably didn't think about this case.

In the deploy dialog one can switch between accounts, so this switch is different from the drop down list, and if you didn't choose the right one, the dialog cannot find the existing app info based on server name.

I found the drop down list before but didn't find the use of it, since all the items in it is same by name.

I guess users are not expected to deploy same app to different accounts in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the design is understandable.

messages.subject_clean: With multiple accounts, RStudio cannot update existing app
messages.body_plain:
That's good news!

I realized how this works now:

1. the drop down list came from the .dcf files found in app directory
2. with the drop down item selected, the site/account/app info was put on top of the list (so when you chose different item, the order of server will change), and it can be updated.
3. other server in list can only create new app.

Before I found out the drop down list(I found it but didn't understand what it is since they have same name), my intuitive understanding is

1. when I switched between server/accounts, some of them remembered the previous deployment entry, some don't.
2. because the "create new" and "update previous" used same UI, I didn't realize the "update previous" must rely on the drop down list selection, which is not visible in the dialog if not noticed.

I'll suggest to use a different design:

1. the drop down list should be a part of dialog. selecting drop down list need several careful clicks, and you still need to check the dialog after the selection.
2. in the dialog, all drop down items should be inside a panel called "previous deployment", selecting items will show detail of deployment, and user can update (or edit if it's possible) it.
3. there should be another panel/button "create new deployment", user can create new deployment by selecting servers, input app details.

messages.subject: Re: How to make shinyapps.io connect to Microsoft sql server with RODBC work?
messages.subject_clean: How to make shinyapps.io connect to Microsoft sql server with RODBC work?
messages.body_plain:
In your connection string, the separators are supposed to be semi-colon, https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms722656(v=vs.85).aspx?  check the punctuation between the server value and the port value...   e,g, we have a shiny app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> successfully communicating with a SQL db and our connect string looks like:
dbcon_dev_shiny <- odbcDriverConnect("Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=7.4;Server=xx.xx.xxx.xxx;Port=1433;Database=yyyyyyyy;Uid=zzzzz;Pwd=aaaaaaaaa;")

I can't explain why your string would run locally, however, if this is in fact the issue....

# Define server logic for random distribution application
shinyServer(function(input, output)

{

    # One thing I needed was to incorporate a dynamic code because
    # some years had first and second round, but others not
    # I used render UI
    ##  Render UI - Getting Round depending on Year
    output$Round = renderUI({

        round = ifelse( input$Year == 1989 | input$Year == 1993, "Unique",
                        as.data.frame(c("First","Ballotage")))
        round = as.data.frame(round)
        selectInput("Round","Step 2: Select a round:", round[,1])
    })

    # I also used Render UI because I did want to display Counties
    # associated to their regions
    # Render UI showing Counties depending on Regions

    output$County <- renderUI({

        A = ifelse(input$Year >= 2008 & input$Region %in% "Arica y Parinacota",
                   as.data.frame(c("Arica","Putre","General Lagos","Camarones")),
                   ifelse(input$Year < 2008 & input$Region %in% "Arica y Parinacota",
                          c("Change year because this region was created in 2007"),
                          ifelse(input$Year>= 2008 & input$Region %in% "Los Ríos",
                                 as.data.frame(c("Corral","Lanco","Los Lagos","Máfil",
                                                 "Mariquina","Paillaco","Panguipulli","Valdivia",
                                                 "Futrono","La Unión","Lago Ranco","Río Bueno")),
                                 ifelse(input$Year< 2008 & input$Region %in% "Los Ríos",
                                        c("Change year because this region was created in 2007"),
                                        datos10 %>%
                                            filter(Year %in% input$Year)  %>%
                                            filter(Round %in% input$Round) %>%
                                            filter(Region %in% input$Region) %>%
                                            group_by(County) %>%
                                            summarise(Votes = sum(Votes)) %>%
                                            as.data.frame()
                                 ))))
        counties = as.data.frame(A)
        selectInput("County", "Step 4: Select a county:", counties[,1])
    })

    ### I start preparing the data for the different tabs
    # National level calculations, depending on Year and Round
    # I get the National results

    datos1N = reactive({
    datos88 = datos10 %>%
        filter(Year %in% input$Year) %>%
        filter(Round %in% input$Round)
    datosN1 = datos88 %>%
        group_by(Candidate) %>%
        summarise(Votes = sum(Votes)) %>%
        arrange(-Votes)
    datosN1 = as.data.frame(datosN1)
        })

    # Depending on Year, Round and show regional results for all the regions
    # Regional level calculations
    datos1R = reactive({
    datos77 = datos10 %>%
        filter(Year %in% input$Year) %>%
        filter(Round %in% input$Round)%>%
        filter(Region %in% input$Region)
    datosR1 = datos77 %>%
        group_by(Candidate) %>%
        summarise(Votes = sum(Votes)) %>%
        arrange(-Votes)
    datosR1 = as.data.frame(datosR1)

    })

    # I need to get County first
    # County level calculations
    datos1C = reactive({
                datos33 = datos10 %>%
                filter(Year %in% input$Year) %>%
                filter(County %in% input$County) %>%
                filter(Round %in% input$Round)
                datos51 = datos33 %>%
                    group_by(Candidate) %>%
                    summarise(Votes = sum(Votes)) %>%
                    arrange(-Votes)
                datos52 = as.data.frame(datos51)
                n = nrow(datos52)
                datos45 = datos33[1:n,]
                datos46 = datos45 %>%
                select(1:4)
                datos48 = cbind(datos46, datos52)

    })

    # Calculating the votes for the two leading candidates of each Round
    # and each Year
    datosTR1 = reactive({
            datosA = datos10 %>%
            filter(Year %in% input$Year) %>%
            filter(Round %in% input$Round)
            datosA1 = datosA %>%
            group_by(Candidate) %>%
            summarise(Votes=sum(Votes)) %>%
            arrange(-Votes)
            datosA1 = as.data.frame(datosA1)
            datosB = datosA %>%
            group_by(Candidate, Region,Region_ID) %>%
            summarise(Votes=sum(Votes)) %>%
            arrange(-Votes)
            datosB = as.data.frame(datosB)
            datosC = datosB %>%
            filter(Candidate %in% datosA1[1,1])
        })

    datosTR2 = reactive({
            datosA = datos10 %>%
            filter(Year %in% input$Year) %>%
            filter(Round %in% input$Round)
            datosA1 = datosA %>%
            group_by(Candidate) %>%
            summarise(Votes=sum(Votes)) %>%
            arrange(-Votes)
            datosA1 = as.data.frame(datosA1)
            datosB = datosA %>%
            group_by(Candidate, Region,Region_ID) %>%
            summarise(Votes=sum(Votes)) %>%
            arrange(-Votes)
            datosB = as.data.frame(datosB)
            datosC = datosB %>%
            filter(Candidate %in% datosA1[2,1])
    })

    ###### This code prepare the data for the tournout details
    dat2N = reactive({

        tab3 = Par %>%
            filter(Year %in% input$Year) %>%
            filter(Round %in% input$Round)

            filter(Round %in% input$Round)

            summarise(Votes=sum(Votes))

        Vot1 =c(votes1)
        Population = Par %>%
            filter(Year %in% input$Year)%>%
            filter(Round %in% input$Round)
        pie2 = data.frame(Vot1,Population)
        Item = c("Tournout","Not voting")
        Total =c(Vot1,pie2$VAP-Vot1)
        pie3 = data.frame(Item,Total)
        pie3
    })

#######################################################################

    # Generate outputs

    ########################### Tab 1: National level ##

        output$view1 = renderGvis({
            validate(
                need(input$Round != '', 'Please choose a Year, Round, Region and County !')
            )
             bar1 = gvisBarChart (datos1N(),
                        xvar="Candidate", yvar="Votes")
                                })

        output$tab1 =  renderTable({

                need(input$Round != "" , 'Please choose a Year, Round, Region and County !')
            )
            data.frame(dat2N())
        })

                need(input$Round != '', 'Please choose a Year, Round, Region and County !')
            )

                               options=list(width=400, height=225))
        })

    ##################################  Tab 2 Regional ####################

         output$textR1 <- renderText({

            a1 = paste("Votes for candidate (in red):",
                       datosTR1()[1,1])

        })
        output$textR2 <- renderText({
            validate(
                need(input$Year != "", 'Please choose a Year and a Round!'),
                need(input$Round != "", 'Please choose a Year and a Round!')
            )
            a2= paste("Votes for candidate (in blue):",
                      datosTR2()[1,1])

        })

        output$view4 = renderGvis({
            validate(
                need(input$Region != "", "Please choose a Region!")
            )
            gvisColumnChart (datosTR1(),

                                 legend="none",

                                 title="Votes by Region", vAxis="{title:'Votes'}",
                                 hAxis="{title:'Regions'}",
                                 colors= "['#cd3333']",
                                 width=1000, height=300))
        })

        output$view5 = renderGvis({

            gvisColumnChart (datosTR2(),
                             xvar="Region", yvar="Votes",
                             options=list(
                                 legend="none",
                                 lineWidth=2, pointSize=0,
                                 title="Votes by Region", vAxis="{title:'Votes'}",
                                 hAxis="{title:'Regions'}",
                                 colors= "['#0000FF']",
                                 width=1000, height=300))
        })

########################## Tab 3 Maps ###################################################

        output$cand1 <- renderText({

            a1 = paste("Votes for candidate (in red):",
            datosTR1()[1,1])

     })

    output$cand2 <- renderText({

           a2= paste("Votes for candidate (in blue):",
              datosTR2()[1,1])

    })

        output$maps <- renderGvis({

                map1 = gvisGeoChart(datosTR1(),
                 locationvar="Region_ID", colorvar="Votes", hovervar = "Region",
                 options=list(region="CL", displayMode="regions",
                              resolution="provinces",keepAspectRatio = TRUE,
                              datalessRegionColor = "#fcfcfc",
                              colorAxis="{colors:['#ffebcd', '#cd3333']}"
                                ))
                map2 = gvisGeoChart(datosTR2(),
                 locationvar="Region_ID", colorvar="Votes", hovervar = "Region",
                 options=list(region="CL", displayMode="regions",
                              resolution="provinces",keepAspectRatio = TRUE,
                              datalessRegionColor = "#fcfcfc",
                              colorAxis="{colors:['#FFFFFF', '#0000FF']}"
                               ))
                merge = gvisMerge(map1,map2,horizontal=TRUE,tableOptions="cellspacing=10")

                return(merge)

                })
        ########################## Tab 4 - pie Regional

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Just to share my solution.

Checking different sites I found that it did not present the same error if I changed in the code "library(dplyr)" for "require(dplyr)". Then dplyr was recognized.

However, it resulted then that there were more errors and it did not recognize some functions. So I changed them. For example, it did not recognize the function read.xlsx so I installed readxl. After several hours, it finally it is up and running.

Hope this is useful for someone who finds the same problem.

Good luck !

rJava is used by xlsx.

messages.subject_clean: Unable to deploy shiny app due to unable to retrieve package records
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I wrote a shiny app that runs perfectly fine on my local machine, but when I try to deploy it from RStudio, it gives me the following error.

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading bundle for application: 198933...Error: Unable to retrieve package records for the following packages:
- "grDevices", "graphics", "grid", "methods", "stats", "tools", "utils"
Execution halted

Usually I would try to look for a solution online but I can't seem to fine any. I have tried redirecting the libPath, copying the base libraries to a new location and pointing libPaths and wd to it, but to no avail.

The problem is that the packages are base packages of R and I am not able to install it from CRAN or github. My sessioninfo is as follows:

Any ideas would be much appreciated!

Thanks
Justin

messages.body_plain:
HI Justin,

I too got the same problem today. but when i went over the link "https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/227057448-Are-there-any-limitations-to-the-packages-I-can-use-in-an-app-I-deploy-to-shinyapps-io-" i got to know that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service supports deploying packages installed from CRAN, GitHub (both public and private repos), and BioConductor only. if any of your packages in the app you are trying to build are installed from any other source other than CRAN/GITHUB or BioConductor  the the app will not work.

messages.subject: Re: Exporting ggvis plots
messages.subject_clean: Exporting ggvis plots
messages.body_plain:
Martin,

I'm sorry, it turns out I do not have any working ggvis export examples any more. Export relies on a Javascript library (Vega) that I no longer have installed, following an operating system upgrade. The R portion of the code is rather trivial:

library(ggvis)
mtcars %>% ggvis(x = ~wt) %>% export_png(file = "/tmp/myplot.png")

The bulk of the work is installing Vega (and any other required external libraries, which I've since forgotten). The reason for my original post here is that, at least of when I wrote it, Vega was not installed on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>; so export worked in my development copy locally but not in the production copy.

For what it's worth, my current version handles plots as follows (using the ggplot2 and plotly libraries):

Server
---------
p <- ggplot(...)
output$myplot <- p $%>% plotly(...) %>% renderPlotly(...)
ggsave("/tmp/myplot", plot = p)

UI
---
plotlyOutput("myplot", ...)

Paul

messages.subject: Deploying Shiny apps - ZAP reports SQL injection potential
messages.subject_clean: Deploying Shiny apps - ZAP reports SQL injection potential
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

I am not a security expert, though do generally understand best practices.

We have run OWASP's ZAP <https://www.owasp.org/index.php/OWASP_Zed_Attack_Proxy_Project> against an internal version of Shiny and it reports "SQL injection may be possible."

It executed this path /__sockjs__/n=ff4dzvU6tYWSOoEtGf/730/thf2rse9/xhr?query=query%27+AND+%271%27%3D%271%27+--+

Our server returned a 405 without any data, so it would seem okay.

curios if others have tested Shiny for security and what they've found.

Also curious whether anyone has insights into this report

Beyond this, happy to report that ZAP at least thinks Shiny is secure.

messages.body_plain:
It appears you are attempting to deploy a static site to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, which it turns out we don't support.

On Monday, July 31, 2017 at 9:31:48 AM UTC-4, Dorris Scott wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I have been trying to deploy my Shiny app to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and I have been getting a timeout error. Here is what is in my console along with my session information. I only found one question similar to this: https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/206237548-App-upload-timeout-error-for-leaflet. Based on this information, I tried deploying it later on in the day and the following day and it didn't work. If anyone could help me with this matter, it would be much appreciated!
